checks: The continuous gamma density extended by zero is globally Lipschitz for every integer k≥2. The coefficient sum forces at least one nonzero phase, hence Y>0 almost surely. The bounded difference quotient gives differentiation at zero even for k=2, where the density has a corner at the origin.

The normalizer L factors over phases. Tilting a phase of mean b by e^(−y) gives mean b/(1+b), and deterministic zero phases stay at zero. The integer moments in the multinomial expansion give L r! h_r. The factorials cancel in the derivative to give L(h_{k−2}−h_{k−1}), which is p(k−2)−p(k−1).

At n=k−1 one has 1≤n≤μ−b_max. Equality in the geometric comparison forces μ−b_max=k−1 and equality of all positive means. Since μ≥k and b_max≤1, this entails μ=k and b_max=1, hence exactly k unit coefficients. The same configuration satisfies the geometric equality conditions in the converse direction.
